page: Google Cloud Platform c4n-highmem-96 is an x86_64 instance type within the Network Optimized family. It provides 96 dedicated virtual CPUs and 744.0 GB of system memory, which yields an allocation of 7.75 GB of RAM per vCPU core. The platform does not incorporate integrated graphics processing units, operating purely on dedicated host CPU processing cores.

Storage and network configurations are purely disaggregated. The instance includes no local storage drives, requiring all root file systems and application volumes to be provisioned through remote network-attached disks. Additionally, the instance provides zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses, requiring the configuration of Cloud NAT or assigned external IP addresses for external network access.

The hardware configuration achieves a high memory density profile without the financial overhead of attached physical GPUs or local NVMe drives. The primary design tradeoff is complete dependence on network performance for storage I/O operations. Best-fit use cases include distributed in-memory databases, large-scale caching nodes, real-time analytics pipelines, and memory-bound enterprise applications.
description: Google Cloud Platform c4n-highmem-96 is a dedicated x86_64 instance belonging to the Network Optimized family. It offers 96 dedicated virtual CPUs combined with 744.0 GB of system RAM, yielding a high memory density of 7.75 GB per core. The instance operates without bundled hardware accelerators or local storage disks, requiring network-attached storage solutions for all persistence needs. In addition, no complimentary public IPv4 addresses are assigned by default. The high memory capacity combined with dedicated multi-core compute resources makes this instance profile well aligned with large in-memory key-value stores, distributed analytics pipelines, enterprise databases, and high-concurrency memory-intensive applications that require consistent compute performance without resource contention.
